papers.title: Assessing the Climate and Habitability of Tidally Locked Rocky Exoplanets
papers.abstract: Tidally locked exoplanets orbiting M dwarf stars are prime targets in the search for habitable worlds, yet their complex climate dynamics challenge conventional models of habitability. We homogeneously estimated the liquid-water habitability of exoplanets with the highest up-to-date Earth-similarity index. We modified the climate model PLASIM to apply it to tidally locked exoplanets across a range of parameters. We systematically classified and compared potentially habitable exoplanets and selected among the ones featuring the highest Earth-similarity index in the conservative sample of the Habitable Wolds Catalog, both relative to each other and as a function of atmospheric pressure. Our analysis revealed three main climate regimes: Snowball, Hot, and Eyeball planets-the latter having a warm and habitable substellar region with T > 273 K and a localized hydrological cycle. Although surface temperature generally increases with pressure, Eyeball planet climates remain stable in a wide pressure range. Complex atmospheric dynamics govern the behavior of the climate, highlighting the need for detailed climate simulations to guide future observations.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Imagine a planet that always shows the same face to its sun, the way the Moon always shows the same face to Earth. One side is in permanent daylight and the other in permanent night. Such "tidally locked" worlds are common around M dwarfs, which are small, dim, cool stars. Because those stars are so common, these planets are some of the most promising places to look for life beyond our solar system. But their weather works very differently from Earth's, so the usual rules for judging whether a planet can hold liquid water don't always apply. Liquid water is the key ingredient for life as we know it.

**What They Did**
The researchers started with the planets that score highest on the Earth-similarity index, a rating of how much a world resembles our own. They took them from the conservative sample of the Habitable Worlds Catalog. They then modified a climate model called PLASIM, which simulates atmosphere and weather the way a weather forecast does, but for alien planets. They ran it on tidally locked rocky planets across a range of conditions, including different atmospheric pressures. This let them compare the planets with one another in a consistent way.

**Key Findings**
The simulations produced three main kinds of climate. "Snowball" planets are frozen. "Hot" planets are too warm. "Eyeball" planets look like a giant eye. They have a warm patch facing the star, with temperatures above 273 K (the freezing point of water), surrounded by ice. That warm patch has its own local water cycle. Surface temperature generally rises as atmospheric pressure increases. Eyeball planets, however, keep a steady climate across a wide range of pressures. The behavior of these worlds is governed by complex atmospheric circulation.

**Looking Forward**
The results show that simple estimates are not enough to judge whether these planets are habitable. Detailed climate simulations will be needed to decide which planets telescopes should observe first.

papers.title_tr: Kütle Çekimiyle Kilitlenmiş Kayalık Ötegezegenlerin İklimi ve Yaşanabilirliğinin Değerlendirilmesi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Güneşine hep aynı yüzünü gösteren bir gezegen düşünün; tıpkı Ay'ın Dünya'ya hep aynı yüzünü göstermesi gibi. Bir yüzü sürekli gündüz, diğer yüzü sürekli gecedir. Bu tür "gelgit kilitlenmeli" dünyalar, küçük, sönük ve serin yıldızlar olan M cücelerinin etrafında sıkça bulunur. Bu yıldızlar çok yaygın olduğu için söz konusu gezegenler, Güneş Sistemi'nin dışında yaşam aramak için en umut verici yerler arasındadır. Ancak bu gezegenlerin havası Dünya'dakinden çok farklı işler. Bu yüzden bir gezegenin sıvı su barındırıp barındıramayacağını değerlendirmeye yarayan olağan kurallar her zaman geçerli olmaz. Bildiğimiz yaşam için sıvı su temel bir bileşendir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Araştırmacılar, bir dünyanın bizimkine ne kadar benzediğini gösteren Dünya benzerlik indeksinde en yüksek puanı alan gezegenlerden yola çıktı. Bu gezegenleri Yaşanabilir Dünyalar Kataloğu'nun muhafazakâr örneklemi içinden seçtiler. Ardından PLASIM adlı bir iklim modelini değiştirdiler. Bu model, hava durumu tahminlerinde olduğu gibi atmosferi ve havayı simüle eder, ancak ötegezegenler için çalışır. Modeli, farklı atmosfer basınçları dahil çeşitli koşullarda, gelgit kilitlenmeli kayalık gezegenler üzerinde çalıştırdılar. Böylece gezegenleri birbirleriyle tutarlı bir biçimde karşılaştırabildiler.

**Ana Bulgular**
Simülasyonlar üç ana iklim türü ortaya koydu. "Kartopu" gezegenler donmuş durumdadır. "Sıcak" gezegenler ise fazla ısınmıştır. "Göz" gezegenleri ise dev bir göze benzer. Yıldıza dönük tarafta, çevresi buzla kaplı, sıcaklığı 273 K'nin (suyun donma noktası) üzerinde ılık bir bölge bulunur. Bu ılık bölgenin kendine ait yerel bir su döngüsü vardır. Yüzey sıcaklığı genellikle atmosfer basıncı arttıkça yükselir. Buna karşılık Göz gezegenlerinin iklimi geniş bir basınç aralığında kararlı kalır. Bu dünyaların davranışını karmaşık atmosfer dolaşımı belirler.

**İleriye Bakış**
Sonuçlar, bu gezegenlerin yaşanabilir olup olmadığını anlamak için basit tahminlerin yeterli olmadığını gösteriyor. Teleskopların önce hangi gezegenleri gözlemleyeceğine karar vermek için ayrıntılı iklim simülasyonlarına ihtiyaç duyulacak.

papers.title: Benchmark Brown Dwarfs as Chemical Laboratories: Linking System Bulk Properties to Atmospheric Retrievals
papers.abstract: We present the first atmospheric retrieval analysis of two compositional benchmark mid-L dwarfs -- SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4 and GJ 499 C -- using the Brewster retrieval framework, where the wide benchmark nature of these systems provides independent constraints on age and bulk composition from their stellar primaries. These targets were observed with JWST using NIRSpec Prism and MIRI LRS, providing low-resolution (R 100) spectra between 0.6--14.0 μm with high signal-to-noise ratios (SNR 100 -- 600). For SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4, the retrieved cloud combination of a high-altitude enstatite slab and low-altitude iron deck clouds matches phase-equilibrium predictions based on the primary star's Mg/Si ratio. We retrieve a super-solar C/O = 0.71⁺⁰.⁰¹₋₀.₀₁ and slightly metal-rich [M/H] = 0.22⁺⁰.⁰³₋₀.₀₃. This C/O ratio can only be reconciled with the value inferred for the primary if additional oxygen sequestration beyond the retrieved cloud mass is present, or if there are uncertainties in the adopted opacities or other model deficiencies. The inferred [C/H] and [O/H] are 0.31±0.03 and 0.19±0.03, respectively, which are consistent within the relatively large uncertainties of the host star abundances. For GJ 499 C, the retrieved silicon-monoxide and forsterite slab clouds are difficult to explain with simple phase-equilibrium assumptions, yielding Mg/Si 1.9. We estimate C/O = 0.69⁺⁰.⁰²₋₀.₀₂ and [M/H] = 0.13⁺⁰.⁰⁴₋₀.₀₆. For both objects, the inferred radii of 0.85⁺⁰.⁰¹₋₀.₀₁ RₐthrmJuₚ and 1.00⁺⁰.⁰²₋₀.₀₂ RₐthrmJuₚ and masses of 73.7⁺⁴.⁹₋₉.₂ MₐthrmJuₚ and 68.0⁺⁸.⁵₋₁₂.₇ MₐthrmJuₚ are consistent with evolutionary models and system ages, highlighting the plausibility of our results.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Brown dwarfs are "failed stars." They are too light to burn hydrogen the way the Sun does, yet heavier than giant planets. Their atmospheres resemble those of giant exoplanets, but working out their chemical recipes is hard. Usually we know neither a brown dwarf's age nor its ingredients, so we cannot check whether our methods give the right answer. The two brown dwarfs in this study orbit ordinary stars at wide distances. Each pair formed from the same cloud of gas, so the star's age and composition work like an answer key.

**What They Did**
The team used two instruments on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), NIRSpec Prism and MIRI LRS. These spread the objects' light into a rainbow from 0.6 to 14 micrometres. The detail is fairly coarse, but the signal is very clean. The two targets, SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4 and GJ 499 C, are both "mid-L" dwarfs. The team then ran a retrieval code called Brewster. It works like reverse-engineering a recipe from its taste. It tries many combinations of gases and clouds until the simulated light matches what JWST saw.

**Key Findings**
For SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4, the code found a high-altitude layer of enstatite (a rocky mineral) above a lower iron cloud deck. This matches what chemistry predicts from the host star's magnesium-to-silicon ratio. The carbon-to-oxygen ratio came out at 0.71, and the object is slightly richer in heavy elements than the Sun. This ratio agrees with the star's only if extra oxygen is hidden away beyond the clouds found, or if the models have flaws. For GJ 499 C, the silicon monoxide and forsterite clouds are harder to explain, giving a magnesium-to-silicon ratio near 1.9. Its carbon-to-oxygen ratio is 0.69. The radii (0.85 and 1.00 times Jupiter's) and masses (73.7 and 68.0 Jupiter masses) agree with evolutionary models and the systems' ages.

**Looking Forward**
These results suggest the method gives believable answers, and the benchmark systems show where it falls short. The mismatches point to places where cloud and opacity models need improvement. Better models would let astronomers read the chemistry of isolated brown dwarfs and giant planets more reliably, since those have no star to check against.

papers.title_tr: Kimya Laboratuvarı Olarak Referans Kahverengi Cüceler: Sistemin Toplu Özelliklerini Atmosfer Geri Çıkarımlarına Bağlamak
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Kahverengi cüceler "başarısız yıldızlar" olarak bilinir. Güneş gibi hidrojen yakacak kadar kütleli değildirler, ama dev gezegenlerden daha ağırdırlar. Atmosferleri dev ötegezegenlerinkine benzer, ancak kimyasal tariflerini çözmek zordur. Genellikle bir kahverengi cücenin ne yaşını ne de içeriğini bağımsız olarak bilebiliriz. Bu yüzden yöntemlerimizin doğru sonucu verip vermediğini sınayamayız. Bu çalışmadaki iki kahverengi cüce, sıradan yıldızların etrafında geniş yörüngelerde dolanıyor. Her çift aynı gaz bulutundan doğduğu için yıldızın yaşı ve bileşimi bir cevap anahtarı işlevi görüyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu'nun (JWST) iki aygıtını, NIRSpec Prism ve MIRI LRS'yi kullandı. Bu aygıtlar cisimlerin ışığını 0,6 ile 14 mikrometre arasında bir gökkuşağına ayırdı. Ayrıntı düzeyi görece düşük, ama sinyal çok temiz. İki hedef, SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4 ve GJ 499 C, "orta L" türünden cücelerdir. Ardından ekip Brewster adlı bir geri çıkarım kodu çalıştırdı. Bu kod, bir yemeğin tadından tarifini bulmaya benzer biçimde çalışır. Simüle edilen ışık JWST'nin gördüğüyle eşleşene kadar çok sayıda gaz ve bulut karışımını dener.

**Ana Bulgular**
SDSSJ141659.78+500626.4 için kod, yüksek irtifada bir enstatit (kayaç bir mineral) tabakasının altında daha alçakta bir demir bulut tabakası buldu. Bu, ana yıldızın magnezyum/silisyum oranından kimyanın öngördüğü tabloyla uyuşuyor. Karbon/oksijen oranı 0,71 çıktı ve cisim Güneş'ten biraz daha fazla ağır element içeriyor. Bu oran, yıldızınkiyle ancak bulunan bulutların ötesinde fazladan oksijen gizlenmişse veya modellerde eksikler varsa bağdaşıyor. GJ 499 C'de silisyum monoksit ve forsterit bulutlarını açıklamak daha zor ve magnezyum/silisyum oranı yaklaşık 1,9 çıkıyor. Karbon/oksijen oranı 0,69. Yarıçaplar (Jüpiter'inkinin 0,85 ve 1,00 katı) ve kütleler (73,7 ve 68,0 Jüpiter kütlesi), evrim modelleri ve sistemlerin yaşlarıyla uyumlu.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sonuçlar yöntemin inandırıcı yanıtlar verdiğini düşündürüyor, referans sistemler de yöntemin nerede yetersiz kaldığını gösteriyor. Uyumsuzluklar, bulut ve opaklık modellerinin iyileştirilmesi gereken yerleri işaret ediyor. Daha iyi modeller, gökbilimcilerin yanında denetleyecek yıldız bulunmayan yalnız kahverengi cücelerin ve dev gezegenlerin kimyasını daha güvenilir biçimde okumasını sağlayacaktır.

papers.title: Kepler-50: Two Planets in Close Resonance Perturbed by a Non-transiting Planet
papers.abstract: Kepler-50 has two transiting planets close to the 6:5 commensurability. We analyze transit times measured from Kepler data with dynamical fits. We attribute the residual signal to a near-resonance non-transiting third planet in the system. The parameters of the third planet are degenerate. We identified 55 (15) regions of interest for an exterior (interior) perturber, and characterize system parameters in each region of interest with posterior sampling. We find that removing samples that are not long-term stable provides few additional constraints on posteriors, and that the transit times do not confirm the likely 2-body resonant state of the transiting planets as ≈ 68\% of posterior samples that are likely stable are also likely in libration. We identify a small fraction of samples that are in 3-body libration. Despite the degeneracies, we recover robust, tightly constrained masses for Kepler-50 b and c (2.35⁺⁰.⁴⁸₋₀.₄₃ M⊕ and 4.43⁺⁰.⁴⁵₋₀.₄₉ M⊕, respectively) and strongly detected non-zero relative eccentricity for Kepler-50 b and c with (ec - eb) = -0.045 ± 0.003, and (ec - eb) = -0.030 ± 0.004. These close neighbors are in the radius valley and sub-Neptune by size, respectively (1.750 ± 0.038 R⊕ and 2.079 ± 0.060 R⊕). With one of the closest planet pairs known and one of the closest to first-order commensurability, the Kepler-50 system is an especially valuable benchmark for planet formation theory.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Some planets orbit their stars in a kind of gravitational dance, where the timing of one planet's orbit is tied to its neighbor's. This is called resonance. Kepler-50 hosts two planets in an unusually tight version of this arrangement, close to a 6:5 rhythm. That means that for every six laps by one planet, the other completes about five. These are among the closest planet pairs known, and among the closest to this kind of simple orbital ratio. That makes the system a useful test case for theories of how planets form and settle into their orbits.

**What They Did**
The team used data from the Kepler space telescope, which watched the planets pass in front of their star, an event called a transit. When planets tug on each other, those transits arrive slightly early or late, like a train that keeps running a bit off schedule. The researchers fit these timing shifts with computer models that follow the planets' gravitational pull on each other. The leftover timing signal that two planets could not explain pointed to a third planet that does not transit. Its properties can't be pinned down uniquely, so the team identified 55 candidate regions for a perturber farther out and 15 for one closer in. papers.title_tr: Kepler-50: Transit Yapmayan Bir Gezegenin Etkilediği, Yakın Rezonanstaki İki Gezegen
papers.summary_tr:

Bu çift, bilinen en yakın gezegen çiftleri arasında ve bu tür basit yörünge oranına en yakın olanlardan biri. İki gezegenle açıklanamayan artık sinyal, transit yapmayan üçüncü bir gezegene işaret ediyordu. Bu gezegenin özellikleri tek bir çözüme indirgenemediği için ekip, dışarıda bir gezegen için 55, içeride bir gezegen için 15 aday bölge belirledi. papers.title: The Isotopic and Elemental Abundances of Planet-Host Star TRAPPIST-1
papers.abstract: Elemental and isotopic abundances are key tracers of planet formation, stellar evolution, and Galactic chemical evolution. Very low-mass stars are particularly interesting in this regard, because unlike more massive or evolved stars their photospheric abundances retain the star's natal composition. Cool dwarf spectra have historically been challenging to use for measurements of chemical abundances because of the blending of molecular and atomic features. However, recent advances in molecular line lists, atmospheric models, fitting techniques and IR spectrographs have enabled the successful measurement of elemental and isotopic ratios in a few dozen very low-mass stars. Here, we present near-infrared high-resolution spectroscopy of TRAPPIST-1 covering the fundamental and overtone bands of carbon monoxide and its prominent isotopologues. From the joint analysis of the K-band (CFHT/SPIRou) and M-band (Keck/NIRSPEC) spectra, we derive the first stellar C/O ratio and the first carbon and oxygen isotope ratios for this star. We obtain a metallicity of [M/H] = 0.00 ± 0.06, a C/O ratio of 0.60 ± 0.02, ¹²C/¹³C = 154⁺¹⁷₋₁₆, and ¹⁶O/¹⁸O = 490⁺⁷⁸₋₆₄. TRAPPIST-1 has generally solar-like elemental abundances, with a ¹²C/¹³C ratio that is higher than the solar value and may be modestly elevated relative to some nearby cool dwarfs at similar metallicity. While C/O is most tightly constrained by the K-band, the isotopic detections are driven by the M-band data.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Stars and their planets are born from the same cloud of gas and dust, so a star's chemical makeup works like a family recipe that its planets may share. Scientists use ratios between elements, such as carbon to oxygen, and between different "flavors" (isotopes) of the same element to trace how planets form, how stars age, and how our galaxy's chemistry has changed over time. Very low-mass stars are especially useful for this. Heavier or more evolved stars alter their surfaces over time, but the surfaces of very low-mass stars keep the composition they were born with.

**What They Did**
Measuring the chemistry of cool, small stars is hard. Their light is crowded with overlapping molecular and atomic fingerprints, like many people talking at once. Better molecular line lists, atmosphere models, fitting techniques, and infrared instruments have recently made it possible for a few dozen such stars. The team studied the planet-host star TRAPPIST-1 with high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy, which spreads starlight into a fine rainbow. The spectra covered carbon monoxide and its isotopologues, versions of the molecule built with heavier carbon or oxygen atoms. They combined data from two telescopes: CFHT/SPIRou (Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope) in the K-band and Keck/NIRSPEC in the M-band.

**Key Findings**
This is the first measurement of TRAPPIST-1's carbon-to-oxygen ratio and of its carbon and oxygen isotope ratios. The star's overall metal content matches the Sun's ([M/H] = 0.00 ± 0.06). Its carbon-to-oxygen ratio is 0.60 ± 0.02. It has roughly 154 atoms of carbon-12 for every carbon-13 atom, which is higher than the solar value and may be modestly elevated compared with some nearby cool dwarfs of similar metallicity. It has about 490 atoms of oxygen-16 for every oxygen-18 atom. Overall, the star's elements look broadly solar-like. The K-band data pinned down the carbon-to-oxygen ratio best, while the M-band data drove the isotope detections.

**Looking Forward**
These measurements add TRAPPIST-1 to the small but growing group of very low-mass stars with measured isotope ratios. They also show that combining two infrared wavelength ranges can reveal chemical details that neither range gives alone.

papers.title_tr: Gezegen Barındıran Yıldız TRAPPIST-1'in İzotopik ve Element Bolluğu
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Yıldızlar ve gezegenleri aynı gaz ve toz bulutundan doğar. Bu yüzden bir yıldızın kimyasal bileşimi, gezegenlerinin de paylaşabileceği bir aile tarifi gibidir. Bilim insanları, karbon ve oksijen gibi elementlerin birbirine oranını ve aynı elementin farklı "çeşitlerinin" (izotoplarının) oranlarını kullanarak gezegenlerin nasıl oluştuğunu, yıldızların nasıl yaşlandığını ve galaksimizin kimyasının zaman içinde nasıl değiştiğini izler. Çok düşük kütleli yıldızlar bu iş için özellikle değerlidir. Daha ağır ya da daha evrimleşmiş yıldızlar yüzeylerini zamanla değiştirir, ancak çok düşük kütleli yıldızların yüzeyi doğdukları andaki bileşimi korur.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Soğuk ve küçük yıldızların kimyasını ölçmek zordur. Işıkları, aynı anda konuşan pek çok insanın sesi gibi, üst üste binen molekül ve atom izleriyle doludur. Moleküler çizgi listelerindeki, atmosfer modellerindeki, uyum tekniklerindeki ve kızılötesi tayfölçerlerdeki son gelişmeler, bu ölçümü birkaç düzine yıldız için mümkün kıldı. Ekip, gezegen barındıran yıldız TRAPPIST-1'i yüksek çözünürlüklü yakın kızılötesi tayfölçümle inceledi. Bu yöntem yıldız ışığını ince bir gökkuşağına ayırır. Tayflar karbon monoksit ve onun izotopologlarını, yani daha ağır karbon veya oksijen atomlarıyla kurulmuş biçimlerini kapsıyordu. Ekip iki teleskobun verisini birleştirdi: K bandında CFHT/SPIRou (Kanada-Fransa-Hawaii Teleskobu) ve M bandında Keck/NIRSPEC.

**Ana Bulgular**
Bu çalışma, TRAPPIST-1'in karbon/oksijen oranının ve karbon ile oksijen izotop oranlarının ilk ölçümüdür. Yıldızın genel metal miktarı Güneş'inkiyle uyumludur ([M/H] = 0,00 ± 0,06). Karbon/oksijen oranı 0,60 ± 0,02'dir. Her karbon-13 atomuna karşılık yaklaşık 154 karbon-12 atomu vardır. Bu değer Güneş'inkinden yüksektir ve benzer metalliğe sahip bazı yakın soğuk cücelere göre hafifçe yüksek olabilir. Her oksijen-18 atomuna karşılık ise yaklaşık 490 oksijen-16 atomu düşer. Genel olarak yıldızın elementleri Güneş'e benzer görünür. Karbon/oksijen oranını en iyi K bandı verileri belirledi. İzotop tespitlerini ise M bandı verileri sağladı.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu ölçümler, TRAPPIST-1'i izotop oranları ölçülmüş çok düşük kütleli yıldızların küçük ama büyüyen grubuna ekliyor. Ayrıca iki farklı kızılötesi dalga boyu aralığını birleştirmenin, tek başına hiçbirinin veremeyeceği kimyasal ayrıntıları ortaya çıkarabildiğini gösteriyor.

papers.title: Discovery and Characterization of the TOI-4468 Planetary System: A Transiting Hot Jupiter With a Lone Nearby Outer Companion
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of two planets, a hot Jupiter and a nearby outer sub-Neptune, orbiting the star TOI-4468. This system is unique among the current exoplanet census in that it features a close outer companion to a hot Jupiter without an accompanying inner companion. By jointly fitting radial velocity measurements taken with the NEID spectrograph and transit photometry from TESS and several ground-based observatories, we constrain the orbital periods, masses, and radii of these two planets. We confirm the planetary nature of the hot Jupiter TOI-4468 b (R = 1.01 R_J, m = 0.54 M_J, P = 2.77 days). We also validate the outer planet TOI-4468 c (R = 0.28 R_J, P = 7.01 days) statistically, incorporating constraints from ground-based observations. We also identify, but cannot confirm, an additional radial velocity signal which may be due to an outer giant in this system with an orbital period of 624 days. From the observed geometry of this system, we argue that it must never have encountered an early secular resonance that is thought to excite the mutual inclination of other hot Jupiter/outer companion systems. We discuss the possibility of an undetected inner companion, as well as potential implications for hot Jupiter formation.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Hot Jupiters are giant planets that circle their stars in just a few days, far closer than Mercury is to our Sun. Astronomers still debate how they ended up so close, since such a scorching spot is a hard place for a giant planet to form. One clue is which other planets share the neighborhood. The newly studied star TOI-4468 is unusual. Its hot Jupiter has a close neighbor farther out but no detected neighbor closer in. No other known system has this arrangement, which makes it a rare test case for theories of how hot Jupiters arrive where they are.

**What They Did**
The team combined two kinds of measurements. First, they used a spectrograph called NEID, which spreads starlight into a rainbow so that tiny back-and-forth wobbles in the star's motion can be detected. Those wobbles are caused by the gravitational tug of orbiting planets. Second, they used transit photometry, which tracks the slight dimming of a star when a planet passes in front of it. These data came from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and several ground-based observatories. They fitted all the data together to work out each planet's orbit, mass, and size.

**Key Findings**
The hot Jupiter, TOI-4468 b, is about the same size as Jupiter (1.01 times its radius) but only about half as massive (0.54 times), and it orbits every 2.77 days. The second planet, TOI-4468 c, is much smaller, about 0.28 Jupiter radii, and is classed as a sub-Neptune. It orbits every 7.01 days. It was validated statistically rather than confirmed by direct mass measurement. The team also saw a hint of another signal in the wobble data, possibly from a giant planet on a 624-day orbit, but they cannot confirm it. From the system's geometry, they argue it never went through an early gravitational "tug-of-war" (a secular resonance) that is thought to tilt the orbits of companions in other hot Jupiter systems.

**Looking Forward**
The authors discuss whether a smaller planet closer in might be hiding undetected. Further observations could also test the possible 624-day giant. Either result would sharpen our understanding of how hot Jupiters form and what happens to their neighbors.

Astronomers still debate how they ended up so close, since such a scorching spot is a hard place for a giant planet to form. One clue is which other planets share the neighborhood. The newly studied star TOI-4468 is unusual. Its hot Jupiter has a close neighbor farther out but no detected neighbor closer in. No other known system has this arrangement, which makes it a rare test case for theories of how hot Jupiters arrive where they are.

What They Did

The team combined two kinds of measurements. First, they used a spectrograph called NEID, which spreads starlight into a rainbow so that tiny back-and-forth wobbles in the star's motion can be detected. Those wobbles are caused by the gravitational tug of orbiting planets. Second, they used transit photometry, which tracks the slight dimming of a star when a planet passes in front of it. These data came from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and several ground-based observatories. They fitted all the data together to work out each planet's orbit, mass, and size.

Key Findings

The hot Jupiter, TOI-4468 b, is about the same size as Jupiter (1.01 times its radius) but only about half as massive (0.54 times), and it orbits every 2.77 days. The second planet, TOI-4468 c, is much smaller, about 0.28 Jupiter radii, and is classed as a sub-Neptune. It orbits every 7.01 days. It was validated statistically rather than confirmed by direct mass measurement. The team also saw a hint of another signal in the wobble data, possibly from a giant planet on a 624-day orbit, but they cannot confirm it. From the system's geometry, they argue it never went through an early gravitational "tug-of-war" (a secular resonance) that is thought to tilt the orbits of companions in other hot Jupiter systems.

Looking Forward

The authors discuss whether a smaller planet closer in might be hiding undetected. Further observations could also test the possible 624-day giant. Either result would sharpen our understanding of how hot Jupiters form and what happens to their neighbors.

papers.summary_tr:

Böylesine kavurucu bir bölge dev bir gezegenin oluşması için zor bir yer olduğundan, gökbilimciler bu gezegenlerin yıldızlarına bu kadar nasıl yaklaştığını hâlâ tartışıyor. papers.title: JWST color sequence of transiting exoplanets and directly imaged substellar objects
papers.abstract: Color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) have been foundational across astrophysics, from galaxies and stars to brown dwarfs, and JWST now extends them to transiting exoplanets and self-luminous substellar objects at overlapping temperatures. We compile JWST dayside emission spectra for 13 transiting giant planets, 57 self-luminous objects, and the irradiated brown dwarf ZTF J0038+2030 B, spanning 350-2600 K and log g = 2.5-5.5, plus 2150 SPHEREx ultracool dwarfs, converted to synthetic photometry in 2MASS J/Ks and five NIRCam medium bands isolating H2O, CH4, CO2, and CO. Low gravity and inflated radii make transiting planets resemble young substellar objects, with shallower features and redder colors from high-altitude clouds that raise the photosphere. Transiting planets follow the L-dwarf sequence on the J versus J-K CMD, with WASP-80 b (Tₑq 800 K) showing no T-dwarf-like blueward turn, suggesting a delayed or suppressed L/T transition in irradiated, low-gravity atmospheres. Methane onset is delayed from substellar to transiting-planet atmospheres, and cloudy radiative-convective models indicate that lower gravity and cloud back-warming shift atmospheres toward CO-dominated chemistry, suppressing photospheric CH4. The irradiated but old, high-gravity brown dwarf ZTF J0038+2030 B (Tday = 1049 K, log g = 5.4) shows a deep, field-T-dwarf-like dayside methane band, implicating gravity rather than irradiation as the dominant control. CO2-to-CO diagnostics place transiting and directly imaged planetary-mass companions at stronger relative CO2 absorption than field brown dwarfs, consistent with metallicity enhancement from planetesimal accretion. These CMD sequences provide a unified, model-testable map for self-luminous and irradiated atmospheres.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Astronomers have long sorted stars by plotting how bright they are against how red or blue they look. This "color-magnitude diagram" works like a family photo album arranged by age and size, and it reveals how stars, brown dwarfs, and galaxies are related. Brown dwarfs are objects too big to be planets but too small to shine as true stars. Until now, nobody could easily place planets orbiting other stars on the same chart as these objects. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is now making that comparison possible, because transiting giant planets and free-floating or distant substellar objects overlap in temperature.

**What They Did**
The team gathered JWST measurements of daytime-side light from 13 transiting giant planets (planets that pass in front of their stars). They added 57 self-luminous objects, meaning brown dwarfs and young planet-like bodies that glow with their own heat. They also included one irradiated brown dwarf, ZTF J0038+2030 B, and 2,150 ultracool dwarfs observed by the SPHEREx telescope. Together these span roughly 350 to 2600 kelvin. The researchers turned all the spectra into simple brightness measurements in a few color filters, including ones that pick out water, methane, carbon dioxide, and carbon monoxide.

**Key Findings**
Transiting planets look like young, low-gravity brown dwarfs: puffier, with muted spectral features and redder colors, likely because high clouds hide deeper layers. They follow the "L-dwarf" sequence, and WASP-80 b (about 800 K) did not make the blueward turn that cooler brown dwarfs do. This suggests that this transition is delayed or suppressed in irradiated, low-gravity atmospheres. Methane appears later in planets, and models suggest low gravity and cloud warming favor carbon monoxide over methane. The old, dense, irradiated brown dwarf ZTF J0038+2030 B (about 1049 K) showed a strong methane band like ordinary field brown dwarfs, pointing to gravity rather than starlight as the main control. Finally, planets and planetary-mass companions show relatively more carbon dioxide absorption than field brown dwarfs, consistent with extra heavy elements from swallowed planetesimals.

**Looking Forward**
These color maps give theorists a shared benchmark for testing atmosphere models of both glowing and starlight-heated worlds.

papers.title_tr: Transit yapan ötegezegenlerin ve doğrudan görüntülenen alt yıldız cisimlerinin JWST renk dizisi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gökbilimciler uzun zamandır yıldızları, ne kadar parlak olduklarına ve ne kadar kırmızı ya da mavi göründüklerine göre grafiğe döker. "Renk-parlaklık diyagramı" denen bu grafik, yaşa ve boyuta göre dizilmiş bir aile albümü gibidir ve yıldızların, kahverengi cücelerin ve gökadaların birbiriyle ilişkisini ortaya koyar. Kahverengi cüceler, gezegen olamayacak kadar büyük, gerçek bir yıldız gibi parlayamayacak kadar küçük cisimlerdir. Şimdiye kadar başka yıldızların etrafındaki gezegenleri bu cisimlerle aynı grafiğe yerleştirmek kolay değildi. James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) bu karşılaştırmayı mümkün kılıyor, çünkü transit yapan dev gezegenler ile alt yıldız cisimlerinin sıcaklıkları örtüşüyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, transit yapan (yıldızlarının önünden geçen) 13 dev gezegenin gündüz tarafından gelen ışığa ilişkin JWST ölçümlerini bir araya getirdi. Buna kendi ısısıyla parlayan 57 cismi ekledi; bunlar kahverengi cüceler ve genç, gezegen benzeri cisimlerdir. Ayrıca yıldız ışığıyla ısınan kahverengi cüce ZTF J0038+2030 B'yi ve SPHEREx teleskobunun gözlediği 2.150 ultraserin cüceyi de dahil ettiler. Bu cisimler yaklaşık 350 ile 2600 kelvin arasındaki sıcaklıkları kapsıyor. Araştırmacılar tüm tayfları, su, metan, karbondioksit ve karbonmonoksiti seçen filtreler de dahil olmak üzere birkaç renk filtresinde basit parlaklık ölçümlerine dönüştürdü.

**Ana Bulgular**
Transit yapan gezegenler genç, düşük çekimli kahverengi cücelere benziyor: daha şişkinler, tayf çizgileri daha sönük ve renkleri daha kırmızı. Bunun nedeni muhtemelen derin katmanları gizleyen yüksek bulutlar. Gezegenler "L cücesi" dizisini izliyor; yaklaşık 800 K sıcaklığındaki WASP-80 b ise daha soğuk kahverengi cücelerde görülen maviye doğru dönüşü yapmadı. Bu, söz konusu geçişin ışınıma maruz kalan, düşük çekimli atmosferlerde gecikmiş ya da bastırılmış olabileceğini düşündürüyor. Metan gezegenlerde daha geç beliriyor; modeller, düşük çekimin ve bulutların sağladığı ek ısınmanın metan yerine karbonmonoksiti öne çıkardığını gösteriyor. Yaşlı, yoğun ve ışınıma maruz kalan kahverengi cüce ZTF J0038+2030 B (yaklaşık 1049 K) ise sıradan alan kahverengi cüceleri gibi güçlü bir metan bandı gösterdi; yani asıl belirleyici yıldız ışığı değil, çekim. Son olarak gezegenler ve gezegen kütleli yoldaşlar, alan kahverengi cücelerine göre görece daha güçlü karbondioksit soğurması sergiliyor. Bu, yutulan gezegenciklerden gelen ek ağır elementlerle uyumlu.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu renk haritaları, hem kendi ışığıyla parlayan hem de yıldız ışığıyla ısınan dünyaların atmosfer modellerini sınamak için kuramcılara ortak bir ölçüt sunuyor.
